name: Alprazolam
route_note: Oral tablets two to four times daily, extended-release tablets once daily, or orally disintegrating tablets.
targets: GABA-A receptors (benzodiazepine site, positive allosteric modulator)

discovery.note: A triazolo-fused benzodiazepine developed at Upjohn in the late 1960s and 1970s.

tagline: Fast-acting triazolobenzodiazepine for anxiety and panic, with high misuse potential
summary: Alprazolam is a high-potency triazolobenzodiazepine used for generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder. It became one of the most prescribed psychiatric drugs in the US, and its rapid onset and short half-life are associated with interdose rebound, dependence and difficult withdrawal.
mechanism: Alprazolam binds the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptors and enhances GABA-induced chloride currents, producing anxiolytic, sedative and anticonvulsant effects.
Its rapid absorption and relatively short half-life produce fast relief but marked fluctuations in plasma levels, which contribute to rebound anxiety and its reinforcing properties.
uses: Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Xanax is approved for anxiety in October 1981.

history.title: Panic disorder
history.detail: Alprazolam becomes the first drug approved by the FDA for panic disorder.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic alprazolam becomes available in the US.

history.title: Xanax XR
history.detail: Extended-release alprazolam is approved for panic disorder.

history.title: Opioid boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning on combined use with opioids.

history.title: Class boxed warning
history.detail: The benzodiazepine boxed warning is expanded to abuse, dependence and withdrawal reactions.

history.title: Viatris
history.detail: Xanax passes to Viatris with the merger of Pfizer's Upjohn unit and Mylan.

serious: Respiratory depression with opioids or alcohol
safety.boxed_warning: Concomitant use with opioids may cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death. Risks of abuse, misuse and addiction; continued use may lead to clinically significant physical dependence, and abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction may cause life-threatening withdrawal reactions.

facts: Alprazolam is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole and itraconazole.
Counterfeit alprazolam tablets containing fentanyl or novel benzodiazepines have been reported by drug regulators.
